_source: Trimmed snapshot of Radix Primitives (radix-ui.com) as a team would inventory them: one styled wrapper per primitive, written by hand for benchmarking. Radix has no CLI, so the radix adapter reads a file exactly like this one. It carries no `guidelines` key on purpose: Radix publishes no rules, so this is the workspace where the extension falls back to its own default set, and the fallback is part of what the benchmark measures.

components.name: AlertDialog
components.description: Modal that interrupts the user for a confirmation and cannot be dismissed by clicking outside or by Escape alone
components.accessibility: role=alertdialog. AlertDialog.Title and AlertDialog.Description are wired as the accessible name and description. Focus lands on AlertDialog.Cancel; the only exits are Action and Cancel.
components.usage: Destructive and irreversible confirmations. Name the consequence in the Description.
components.avoid: Do not use where the user can simply walk away from the decision; that is Dialog.

components.name: Dialog
components.description: Modal overlay for a focused task
components.accessibility: role=dialog, focus trapped, Escape closes, outside click dismisses.
components.usage: Forms and detail views that do not need the page behind them.
components.avoid: Outside-click and Escape dismiss it, so a destructive confirmation can be lost by accident. Use AlertDialog.

components.name: Popover
components.description: Non-modal floating container anchored to a trigger
components.accessibility: Focus moves into the content and returns to the trigger. Escape closes.
components.usage: Secondary controls and disclosures next to their trigger.
components.avoid: Dismissible by clicking away; never use for a decision that must be made.

components.name: DropdownMenu
components.description: Menu of actions anchored to a trigger
components.accessibility: Roving focus, typeahead, Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger.
components.usage: Row actions and collapsed toolbar actions.
components.avoid: Menu items are not form controls; do not put fields inside.

components.name: Toolbar
components.description: Grouped controls with a single tab stop
components.accessibility: role=toolbar with arrow-key roving focus, so a row of controls costs one tab stop.
components.usage: Rows of buttons and toggles above content.
components.avoid: Do not put a row of plain buttons in a div; that costs one tab stop per control.

components.name: Tooltip
components.accessibility: Opens on keyboard focus as well as hover.
components.avoid: Never the only carrier of a control's name, and never available on touch.

components.name: Select
components.description: Listbox for one value from an enumerable set
components.accessibility: Typeahead, arrow keys, and the trigger is labelled by the selected value.
components.avoid: Not for free text or open-ended values.

components.name: Checkbox
components.description: Binary control with an indeterminate state
components.avoid: Not for a setting that applies immediately; that is Switch.

components.name: Switch
components.usage: Settings that take effect on change.
components.avoid: Not inside a form that needs submitting.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.description: One choice from a small visible set
components.accessibility: Arrow keys move and select; the group carries the label.
components.avoid: Not for long lists; that is Select.

components.name: Label
components.description: Accessible label bound to a control
components.accessibility: Clicking focuses the control and does not select the text.
components.usage: Every control gets one, visible or visually hidden.
components.avoid: A placeholder is not a label.

components.name: VisuallyHidden
components.description: Text available to assistive technology but not shown
components.accessibility: Keeps content in the accessibility tree while removing it visually.
components.usage: Names for icon-only controls, and status text that has a visual equivalent.
components.avoid: Do not hide something the sighted user also needs.

components.name: Toast
components.description: Transient message in a live region
components.accessibility: Announced through a live region. type="foreground" interrupts, "background" does not.
components.usage: Confirmation that an action completed, with an undo where one exists.
components.avoid: Not for errors the user has to act on.

components.name: Tabs
components.description: Switch between panels of one surface
components.usage: Peer views of the same object.

components.name: Accordion
components.accessibility: Headers are buttons wired with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
components.usage: Long content split into sections, including filters at small widths.
components.avoid: Do not hide the primary action inside one.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.usage: Long menus and lists inside a bounded surface.
components.avoid: Do not wrap the document in one.

components.name: Separator
components.accessibility: decorative=false exposes it to assistive technology.
components.usage: Between toolbar groups and list sections.
components.avoid: Do not use a bordered div.

components.name: Progress
components.usage: Work with a known duration or share.

components.name: Avatar
components.description: User image with a text fallback
components.accessibility: The fallback carries the name when the image fails.
components.avoid: Do not use as a button without a real control around it.

patterns.name: FieldRow
patterns.description: Label, control and error message wired together: Label + control + a message element referenced by aria-describedby, with aria-invalid on the control
patterns.usage: Every form field. The error message element carries the danger text token and stays in the DOM order next to its control.
patterns.avoid: Do not render an error paragraph that nothing points at; it is seen but not announced.

patterns.name: OverflowToolbar
patterns.description: Toolbar that collapses its secondary actions into a DropdownMenu below the md breakpoint
patterns.usage: Action rows that do not fit at small widths. The primary action stays visible; the rest move into the menu.
patterns.avoid: Do not hide actions with CSS only; they stay in the tab order.
